correctness.rationale: The proof reduces spectral orthogonality to a three-unit-vector sum, which forces primitive cube roots; Bezout then gives the exact zero set. The normalized-spectrum classification follows from the three pairwise differences. For tilings, a self-contained invertible finite-state recurrence proves periodicity of any primitive complement, and finite-group Fourier support then forces period three. Residue fibers modulo the gcd give the general classification. The packaged verifier independently exhausts bounded exact finite cases; it is explicitly not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Cardinality three is the first nontrivial prime-size finite Hadamard case and is a natural test case for the recent reduction of one-dimensional Fuglede questions to finite cyclic structure. The result does more than reprove existence: it gives the exact denominator scale, all normalized spectra, all integer tiling complements, and exact moduli counts. That complete low-cardinality structure is a reusable boundary case rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
